svg.title: Network topologies explained — study visual
svg.desc: Study guide on bus, ring, star, and tree network topologies with advantages and disadvantages

g.text: Topology = the virtual shape of a network
Determined by how data moves from one node to another. Types: bus, ring, star, tree.

svg.text: Nodes daisy-chained along one cable (backbone). Resistor at each end stops signal bouncing back.

g.text: Every node "sees" all data → security risk

svg.text: Nodes daisy-chained in a giant ring. Data travels clockwise or counter-clockwise.
A token loops endlessly — node grabs it, replaces it with data + destination address, message circles until recipient found.
Several nodes linked to a central hub, switch, or router. One cable or device fails → others continue working.
Multiple star topologies on a bus. Nodes in areas → hubs → connected along the network backbone.
